correctness.rationale: For 0≤z≤1/2, uniformize Q=2(P-I) with stochastic P and nonnegative degree-four Poisson coefficients. For every four-vertex segment the distance-three entry is z³(4-z sum degrees)/24, forcing 2/3 for n4, 4/7 for n5, and 1/2 for n≥6. All other entries for n4 and n5 are explicitly nonnegative through endpoints: distance-four quartic, distance-two positive discriminant-negative quadratics, distance-one monotone cubics and positive-definite RK4 polynomial diagonals. n2,n3 have strictly monotone cubic factors for nearest-neighbor entries and positive remaining offdiagonals. This is an analytic complete proof; the extracted exact-rational verifier checked 40497 assertions and does not replace the unbounded-size symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The sharp all-size, reflecting-path-specific RK4 endpoint classification was not implied by the inspected full primary literature on universal RK4 positivity radius, invariant subcones, graph-Laplacian integrators, or different heat positivity schemes. The universal RK4 radius is zero (Horváth 1998), yet restricted paths have positive sharp intervals: this model-specific statement needs the four-site walk-degree identity and small-boundary analysis. Search nonhits alone are not proof of publication novelty; a recent inaccessible heat-scheme preprint remains a stated risk. One component is already known: an earlier exact directed-cycle RK4 classification determines the identical two-state cubic because the two generators agree at n=2. This special case is retained only for a complete natural path classification and is not presented as independently novel.

value.rationale: The naturally arising reflective finite-difference heat generator is a principal numerical analysis benchmark. This exact complete grid-size classification reveals an initially surprising boundary-to-interior transition: classical fourth-order RK has strictly larger positivity steps on two through five vertices but cannot beat forward Euler on any path of six or more vertices. The sharp degree-sum mechanism and nontrivial small-size roots provide concrete safety limits for diffusion solvers independent of ordinary RK spectral stability. It does not extrapolate from arbitrary unmotivated finite tabulation.
